TestScyllaSstableDumpData::test_scylla_s.description: Single node, table (name text PK, value_one int, value_two int), inserts 4 rows, flushes, runs `scylla sstable dump-data --merge` via ccm `run_scylla_sstable` (snapshot + schema autodetection, no --schema-file), parses partition key + column values from JSON and compares to the inserted tuples with `ScyllaSstable._compare_data` (scylla_sstable_test.py:42: set symmetric difference must be empty -> exact, order-insensitive). Guards correctness of dump-data JSON content for simple int/text columns; written as feature-parity demo vs C* sstabledump.

origin.summary: Add scylla_sstable_test.py (Botond Denes): mirror of sstabledump_test.py ported to scylla-sstable to show feature parity; depends on scylla-ccm#471 (run_scylla_sstable).

TestScyllaSstableDumpData::test_scylla_s.relevance: Live: scylla-sstable dump-data with --merge and JSON output (tools/scylla-sstable.cc, mutation/json.hh). ccm run_scylla_sstable relies on schema autodetection from the snapshot dir, also live (tools/schema_loader.cc).

Only asserts output non-empty / json.loads; Bug in that test: line 394 hardcodes simple_clustering_table, ignoring its table_factory param.

TestScyllaSstableDumpData::test_scylla_s.reason: Cheap (6s, 100% pass) exact check of dump-data content vs inserted values; scylla cqlpy has only consistency checks (test_metadata_and_value, write_json roundtrip, query_data_types via `query`), none comparing dump-data to ground truth, so overlap is strong but partial. Could be ported to test/cqlpy/test_tools.py. Note (class ScyllaSstable): `_dump_data` (scylla_sstable_test.py:30-40) catches subprocess.CalledProcessError, but ccm run_scylla_sstable raises ccmlib ToolError (scylla-ccm aab335cacf ccmlib/scylla_node.py:1730), so the error-logging branch is dead (ToolError message already has stdout/stderr).

TestScyllaSstableDumpData::test_sstabled.description: Single node, table (pk int PK, cnt counter); for pk 1..9 increments cnt by i and by 10^18, reads expected rows via CQL SELECT, flushes, dumps with `dump-data --merge`, sums counter shard values per cell (`_fetch_counter_data_from_json`, line 131) and compares with base `ScyllaSstable._compare_data` (line 42, exact set equality). Guards dump-data JSON rendering of counter cells/shards, including large (10^18) values.

TestScyllaSstableDumpataAllDatatypes::te.description: Uses CqlshPrepare.all_datatypes_prepare (cqlsh_tests/cqlsh_copy_tests.py:134) to create a table with ~23 column types, drops UDT columns t,u, inserts one row, dumps with `dump-data --merge`, converts each JSON column back to Python (class-local `_fetch_data_from_json`, line 185) and compares positionally with the override `_compare_data` (line 236: `==` per column, only first len(src)-2 columns). TestScyllaSstableDumpataAllDatatypes::te.relevance: Live: dump-data JSON per-type rendering. scylladb#14726 (ff721ec3e3, 2023-07-17) made timestamps end with 'Z', so the add_z=True path is obsolete. The UDT drop workaround references scylla-tools-java#24 (Java sstabledump), irrelevant to scylla-sstable which dumps UDTs (cqlpy clustering_table_with_udt).

duplicates.note: All native types (incl. date/time/duration/smallint/tinyint, not in dtest), collections, UDT, nested UDT vs CQL results, but via `sstable query` not dump-data.

TestScyllaSstableDumpataAllDatatypes::te.reason: Only test checking dump-data JSON per-type values against inserted data, but heavily weakened and partly covered by query_data_types (same types via `query`). Bug: `_compare_data` override (scylla_sstable_test.py:244-245) loops range(len(src)-2), so v/w (nested frozen collections) are never compared; UDT columns t,u dropped (155-158) with stale TODO citing scylla-tools-java#24. Note: add_z workaround (174-183, 190-198) obsolete since scylla ff721ec3e3 (#14726): 'Z'+'Z' parses to a naive datetime with dateutil UnknownTimezoneWarning ('will raise an exception' in future), and that exception would not be AssertionError so the fallback would not catch it. Note: dead CalledProcessError handler in `_dump_data` (ccm raises ToolError).
